title: the scratch tool names a proof scope that moves HOME in-process and leaves USERPROFILE behind
intention: The scratch tool names every proof scope that moves HOME in its own process and leaves USERPROFILE behind, so a scratch HOME on Windows cannot silently read the live one.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akienyoga9i: scratch_home_bypass reads [] over inferenceproxy and aider_shim, while both proofs read the live ~/.cairn on Windows. inferenceproxy's _home did monkeypatch.setenv(HOME) and aider_shim's cold seam string did os.environ[HOME] = %r, and on Windows Path.home() reads USERPROFILE (01414c39eb2b, a0f74572040b). The bypass scan reads env copies handed to a child; an in-process set copies nothing. A census of every proofs/test_*.py at main found exactly those two in-process sites.
traces_to: Law 3; Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics); Law 8.
how: D1: scratch.py gains public scratch_home_in_process(root) -> ['<relpath>:<line> <scope>']: for each function, and each string constant that parses as Python once %r/%s/%d are filled, the env keys it sets in-process (setenv, putenv, os.environ[K]=, os.environ.setdefault/update, patch.dict(os.environ, ...)); named when HOME is set and USERPROFILE is not. A string's lines count from its line in the file. D2: the charter's what names scratch_home_in_process. D3: new proof test_an_in_process_home_move_moves_userprofile_too.py, one tooth per clause, fixture keys spelled apart so the scan does not read the proof itself; the quiet tooth carries a control that must be named.

clauses.claim: each in-process spelling that moves HOME alone is named: setenv, putenv, os.environ[K]=, setdefault, update, patch.dict
the same scopes moving USERPROFILE too are quiet, and so is an env copy handed to a child, while a control is named
a seam string with %r placeholders that moves HOME alone is named at its line in the file
